text:
maria: Heads up — planning canary roll for routing-policy v2 tomorrow during the 15:00-17:00 UTC change window. Targeting a 10% traffic split but want a staged ramp (1% -> 10%). Need SRE + Product approvals and a deploy-bot job scheduled. Any concerns?

deploy-bot: I can schedule that. Example command you can use below. I will enforce the change window and approver list.

jake: 10% sounds reasonable but can we do 1% first, wait 10m health checks, then jump to 10%? avoid noisy spikes.
maria: yes, that's the plan — staged ramp. Also we'll tag requests with X-Canary: routing-v2 for tracing.
ravi: remind folks to warm KV cache and prepopulate the prefix cache. Telemetry dashboard is ready: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/routing-v2 — set the baseline to last-prod.
sara: Product approves on the condition we have an automatic guard + rollback rule for latency and error spikes. Who will own the active monitoring? alex from SRE?
alex: I can own monitoring. Propose rollback thresholds: p50 > +20% over baseline OR error rate +0.5% absolute sustained for 5m -> auto rollback. Also add an alert channel #incidents and webhook to our pager.
jake: +1 for those thresholds. Also recommend a short canary analysis job to run eval prompts and quality checks during stage. If quality drops, we fail fast.
maria: i'll add a quiet-evals set of 50 prompts (linked in the deploy notes) and wire the canary analysis job to fail the deploy if model-level regressions exceed the threshold.
sara: Product approved. Leaving approver in the deploy command as @sara (product) and @alex (SRE).
deploy-bot: here's the command snippet to schedule — copy into #deploy-queue or DM me to schedule:
```bash
/deploy canary routing-v2 \  --stages "1%:10m,10%:20m" \  --window "2026-01-05T15:00Z/2026-01-05T17:00Z" \  --approvers @alex @sara \  --tag X-Canary:routing-v2 \  --rollback "p50:+20% | err:+0.5%:5m" \  --telemetry-dashboard https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/routing-v2
```

ravi: small ask — can we also atomically flip a feature-flag in the console so routing-v2 only affects traffic that opt-in? safer for experiments.
maria: good call. I will create a FF: routing-v2.canary and scope to the canary job.
jake: what about quotas? will the canary consumers hit rate limits differently? need to ensure burst quota is allowed for 10% traffic to avoid 429s.
alex: i'll temporarily bump quota for that route during the window. I'll revert after. deploy-bot, please annotate quota change in the runbook.
deploy-bot: noted — will attach runbook and quota-change entry to the job.
maria: who gives final thumbs? alex and sara confirmed. scheduling now.
sara: :thumbsup: please tag me in the approval request so I get a notification.
marial (typo) -> maria correction: tagging now :)
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary job id 20260105-cc-007, queued for 2026-01-05T15:00Z. Approval requests sent to @alex and @sara. Runbook: https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/20260105-routing-v2-canary
jake: saving the dashboard link and eval links. will monitor p50, p95, and error budget.
ravi: i'll have a warmup job run 10m before window to prime caches.
alex: will standby in #incidents at T-5 and ack approvals once checks look good.
sara: approving now. :white_check_mark:
alex: approved. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: Approvals complete. Job 20260105-cc-007 will start at window. I will post status updates in this thread during rollout (staged ramp, telemetry snapshots, rollback if triggered).
